questions.questionText: Compare a Flashy Storm Hydrograph with a Subdued (Attenuated) Storm Hydrograph in a drainage basin and explain four physical and human basin factors controlling lag time and peak discharge. [25 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [25 marks]
- **Hydrograph Contrast:** Flashy shows short lag time, steep rising limb, high peak discharge; Subdued shows long lag time, gentle rising limb, broad low peak [7 marks].
- **Controlling Factors:** (1) Permeability/rock type (granite/clay boosts overland flow vs porous sandstone percolation); (2) Rainfall intensity vs infiltration capacity (Hortonian overland flow); (3) Basin shape & slope (circular steep basins concentrate flow fast); (4) Land use (urban tarmac/deforestation lowers interception vs dense savanna woodland) [18 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain the Hjulström Curve relationship between river velocity and sediment particle size for erosion, transportation, and deposition, highlighting the anomalous behaviour of clay and silt. [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Curves:** Critical erosion velocity vs settling/deposition velocity against log particle size (0.001 mm – 100 mm) [5 marks].
- **Sand vs Clay Anomaly:** Medium sand (0.1–1 mm) erodes at lowest velocity (~20 cm/s); finer clay/silt particles require unexpectedly HIGH erosion velocities due to strong electrochemical cohesion and smooth bed surface [6 marks]. Once suspended, clay stays transported down to near-zero velocities [4 marks].

questions.questionText: Describe the Tricellular Model of global atmospheric circulation (Hadley, Ferrel, and Polar cells) and explain how seasonal shifts of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) drive Zimbabwe's wet and dry seasons. [25 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [25 marks]
- **Tricellular Model:** Thermal Hadley ascent at equator (0°), subtropical descent (~30° N/S creating Kalahari/Sahara arid belts), Ferrel mid-latitude westerlies, Polar easterlies + Coriolis deflection [13 marks].
- **ITCZ over Zimbabwe:** In austral summer (Nov–Mar), overhead sun shifts south to Tropic of Capricorn, drawing warm moist Congo Air and NE/SE trade convergence over Zimbabwe (convectional rain). In winter (May–Aug), Botswana/Subtropical High dominance brings dry stable descending air [12 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain the formation, vertical structure, and destructive hazards of Tropical Cyclones (e.g., Cyclone Idai, March 2019), and assess how their intensity dissipates inland over eastern Zimbabwe. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Formation:** Sea surface temperatures ≥ 26.5°C, Coriolis force (≥ 5° from equator), low wind shear, latent heat release fueling deep cumulonimbus eyewall around calm subsiding eye [10 marks].
- **Inland Impact & Decay:** Orographic uplift against Chimanimani/Eastern Highlands triggers catastrophic rainfall, landslides, and flash floods before loss of warm ocean moisture and surface friction weaken the storm [10 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain how El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) events alter Walker Circulation over the Pacific and trigger severe agricultural droughts across Southern Africa. [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Normal vs El Niño Walker Cell:** Trade winds weaken/reverse; warm sea surface anomalies shift to central/eastern Pacific, displacing convective ascent eastward [8 marks].
- **Zimbabwe Impact:** Teleconnections strengthen high-pressure subsidence over Southern Africa during peak summer (Dec–Feb), suppressing ITCZ cloud bands and causing mid-season dry spells and crop failure [7 marks].

questions.questionText: With reference to Peltier's weathering diagram, analyse how temperature and precipitation regimes govern chemical versus physical weathering, with specific reference to granite bornhardts (dwalas) and tors in Zimbabwe. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Climate Controls (Peltier):** Chemical weathering (hydrolysis, carbonation, oxidation) dominates in hot, humid climates (doubles rate per +10°C—van't Hoff); physical freeze-thaw/insolation dominates in cold or arid regimes [8 marks].
- **Zimbabwe Granite Landforms (Matobo/Domboshava):** Deep subsurface chemical etching along rectangular joints during humid Tertiary phases followed by stripping of regolith (exhumation/pressure-release sheeting) exposes dome-shaped bornhardts and joint-controlled castle kopjes/tors [12 marks].

questions.questionText: Outline Plate Tectonics theory and compare the landforms and hazards produced at Constructive, Destructive (Subduction), and Collision margins, referencing the East African Rift Valley. [25 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [25 marks]
- **Mechanisms:** Slab pull, ridge push, mantle convection driving lithospheric plates [5 marks].
- **Margins:** Constructive (Mid-Atlantic Ridge / East African Rift horst & graben normal faults, basaltic volcanism); Destructive (ocean trench, Benioff-zone explosive andesitic volcanoes, tsunamis); Collision (Himalayan fold mountains, shallow high-magnitude quakes) [15 marks].
- **East African Rift:** Divergent continental rifting with Lake Tanganyika/Malawi grabens and shield/stratovolcanoes [5 marks].

questions.questionText: Compare Wood's (1942) four-element Slope Profile Model with Young's/King's Pediplanation theory in tropical savanna landscapes. [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Four Slope Elements:** Waxing/convex summit (soil creep), Free face/rock cliff (rockfall/joint control), Constant/debris slope (angle of repose), Waning concave pediment (sheetwash) [8 marks].
- **King's Pediplanation:** Parallel scarp retreat maintains constant steep free-face angle leaving expanding gently concave pediments coalescing into a pediplain dotted with residual inselbergs [7 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain the Gersmehl Nutrient Cycle model and contrast nutrient store sizes and transfer rates between a Tropical Rainforest and a Tropical Savanna (Miombo Woodland) ecosystem. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Gersmehl Stores & Flows:** Biomass, Litter, Soil stores linked by uptake, fallout, decomposition, leaching, weathering [8 marks].
- **Comparison:** Tropical Rainforest holds huge Biomass store with rapid decomposition & intense leaching (thin ferralsols). Miombo Savanna holds much smaller Biomass, larger relative Litter/Soil nutrient retention during dry season, and regular fire mineral-ash recycling [12 marks].

questions.questionText: Define a Soil Catena and explain how topography and drainage create predictable soil property sequences down a Zimbabwean granitic slope (from crest to vlei/dambo). [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Crest/Upper Slope:** Eluviation, thin coarse sandy well-drained red/brown fersiallitic soils [5 marks].
- **Mid-Slope:** Throughflow moves bases & clay downslope; thicker loam profiles [5 marks].
- **Lower Vlei/Dambo:** Illuviation accumulates fine dark vertisol/hydromorphic clay (gleying, anaerobic iron reduction mottling) with high seasonal water table [5 marks].

questions.questionText: Distinguish between River Braiding and River Meandering in alluvial channels, explaining the flow hydraulics (helicoidal flow, thalweg) behind pools, riffles, and point bars. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Braided Channels:** High seasonal sediment load, easily erodible banks, and fluctuating discharge split flow around shifting eyot gravel/sand bars [8 marks].
- **Meanders & Hydraulics:** Pool-and-riffle sequences initiate sinuous thalweg; centrifugal pressure sets up secondary helicoidal corkscrew currents eroding outer river cliffs and depositing sorted inner point bars [12 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain how karst limestone landscapes (such as Chinhoyi Caves) develop through carbonation weathering and fluctuating phreatic water tables. [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Carbonation Chemistry:** Rainwater absorbs CO₂ forming weak carbonic acid (H₂CO₃), dissolving insoluble CaCO₃ into soluble calcium hydrogen carbonate Ca(HCO₃)₂ along bedding planes and vertical joints [8 marks].
- **Landforms:** Limestone pavements, dolines, sinkholes, subterranean caverns below the water table later drained by base-level lowering, and speleothems (stalactites/stalagmites) [7 marks].

questions.questionText: Assess the physical causes of Coastal Erosion and Deposition, explaining the formation of a headland-and-bay sequence, wave-cut platform, and spit. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Erosion Processes:** Hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition, solution + wave refraction concentrating energy on resistant headlands [8 marks].
- **Landforms:** Cliff recession leaves intertidal wave-cut platform; longshore drift transports sediment past coastline bends forming hooked sand spits and salt-marsh lagoons behind them [12 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain atmospheric stability, instability, and conditional instability using Environmental Lapse Rate (ELR), Dry Adiabatic Lapse Rate (DALR), and Saturated Adiabatic Lapse Rate (SALR). [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Rates:** DALR (~9.8°C/km) for unsaturated rising parcels; SALR (~5–6°C/km) above lifting condensation level due to latent heat release [5 marks].
- **Cases:** Absolute stability (ELR < SALR: resists uplift, stratus/fog/inversions); Absolute instability (ELR > DALR: buoyant towering cumulonimbus storms); Conditional instability (SALR < ELR < DALR) [10 marks].

questions.questionText: Evaluate the role of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and Satellite Remote Sensing (NDVI, thermal bands) in monitoring drought, deforestation, and flood hazards in Zimbabwe. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Remote Sensing Capabilities:** Multi-spectral NDVI tracks seasonal vegetation stress/famine early warning; radar/SAR penetrates cloud cover to map Zambezi/Save flood extents; Landsat time-series quantify woodland clearing [10 marks].
- **GIS Integration & Limits:** Overlays elevation DEMs, population density, and road access to target emergency aid; constrained by cloud cover in optical sensors, high-res licensing costs, and ground-truthing needs [10 marks].

questions.questionText: Contrast Urban Heat Island (UHI) microclimates with surrounding rural areas and explain how urban design alters wind, precipitation, and air quality. [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Causes of UHI:** Low albedo dark asphalt/roofs, high thermal capacity brick/concrete, lack of evapotranspiration vegetation, anthropogenic vehicle/AC waste heat [8 marks].
- **Effects:** 2–5°C warmer nocturnal minima, enhanced afternoon convection/downwind storms, canyon street gusts vs overall friction slowdown, photochemical smog inversions [7 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain Plagioclimax and Secondary Succession in ecosystems, using Zimbabwean fire-climax savanna grasslands and abandoned farmland as examples. [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Secondary Succession:** Recolonisation of disturbed land retaining soil/seedbank (pioneer grasses → shrubs → acacia/miombo canopy) [7 marks].
- **Plagioclimax:** Ecosystem arrested from reaching climatic climax by repeated human/biotic disturbance such as annual dry-season burning, grazing, or woodcutting, favouring fire-resistant grasses and thick-barked trees [8 marks].

questions.questionText: Assess the physical causes of Mass Movement (rotational slumping, mudflows, rockfalls) and evaluate two slope-stabilisation engineering measures. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Shear Stress vs Shear Strength:** Heavy rainfall adds pore-water pressure reducing friction, undercutting toes by rivers/roads increases slope angle, seismic shocks/deforestation remove root cohesion [10 marks].
- **Engineering Measures:** Weep-hole sub-surface drainage pipes (reduce pore pressure), rock bolts/gabion retaining walls/shotcrete/terrace grading—evaluate high cost vs effectiveness on Chimanimani mountain highways [10 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain Darcy's Law and distinguish between Confined and Unconfined Aquifers, assessing threats to groundwater sustainability around Harare and Chitungwiza. [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Aquifers:** Unconfined receives direct surface recharge; confined lies trapped beneath impermeable aquiclude creating artesian pressure; Darcy's Law Q = K·A·(dh/dl) [7 marks].
- **Threats:** Uncontrolled urban borehole drilling causing cone-of-depression drawdown, paved surfaces blocking recharge, pit-latrine/industrial leachate contamination [8 marks].

questions.questionText: Evaluate the natural versus anthropogenic drivers of Pleistocene Glacial/Interglacial cycles (Milankovitch orbital forcing) compared with modern Enhanced Greenhouse Global Warming. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Natural Drivers:** Eccentricity (100 kyr), Axial Tilt/Obliquity (41 kyr), Precession (23 kyr), solar variation, volcanic aerosols [8 marks].
- **Anthropogenic Drivers & Evaluation:** Rapid post-industrial rise in CO₂ (>420 ppm), CH₄, and N₂O outpaces natural orbital timescales by orders of magnitude, amplifying positive albedo and permafrost feedbacks [12 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain how Soil Erosion (splash, sheet, rill, and gully erosion) occurs on communal arable slopes and evaluate biological versus mechanical conservation methods. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Mechanisms:** Raindrop detachment (splash) on bare crusted soil → overland sheet flow → concentrated rills → incised headward-advancing dongas/gullies [8 marks].
- **Conservation:** Mechanical (contour ridges, storm drains, gabion check-dams) vs Biological (vetiver grass strips, zero-tillage mulching, agroforestry cover crops) [12 marks].

questions.questionText: Compare Aeolian landforms in hot arid deserts (barchans, seif dunes, yardangs, zeugen) and explain the processes of deflation, saltation, and abrasion. [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Wind Processes:** Deflation hollows out fine dust leaving desert lag pavement; Saltation bounces sand <1.5 m causing basal sandblasting abrasion on mushroom pedestals [7 marks].
- **Landforms:** Crescentic barchans (unidirectional wind, limited sand) vs long linear seif dunes (bimodal winds); streamlined yardangs vs caprock zeugen [8 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain the Water Balance Equation (P = Q + E ± ΔS) and show how seasonal soil moisture budget graphs identify periods of soil moisture surplus, utilisation, deficit, and recharge. [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Equation:** Precipitation = Runoff + Evapotranspiration ± Soil/Groundwater Storage change [5 marks].
- **Four Phases:** When P > PE (rainy season) soil recharges to field capacity then generates runoff surplus; when PE > P (dry season) plants utilise stored moisture until deficit limits growth [10 marks].

questions.questionText: Evaluate the effectiveness of Early Warning Systems, Floodplain Zoning, and Dam Reservoirs (e.g., Tokwe-Mukosi / Kariba) in mitigating fluvial flood hazards. [20 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [20 marks]
- **Hard Engineering (Dams/Levees):** Controls downstream peak flows and generates hydro/irrigation, though expensive, traps silt, and creates catastrophic dam-breach risk if overwhelmed [9 marks].
- **Soft Management (Zoning & Forecasts):** Keeps high-value assets off floodplains and saves lives via early SMS evacuation alerts, though informal settlement enforcement is hard [11 marks].

questions.questionText: Using Spearman's Rank Correlation or Chi-Square concepts in Physical Geography fieldwork, explain how a student tests whether river pebble roundness increases significantly with distance downstream. [15 marks]
questions.explanation:
### Mark Scheme [15 marks]
- **Sampling & Measurement:** Systematic downstream sample sites (10+ sites); random/stratified selection of 20–30 pebbles/site measured on Powers Roundness Scale + Cailleux index [6 marks].
- **Statistical Test (Spearman's rₛ):** Rank distance (x) and mean roundness (y), compute rₛ = 1 − [6Σd² / (n³−n)], compare against critical values at p=0.05/0.01 to accept/reject H₀, noting lithological/tributary caveats [9 marks].
